Imani Brooks: Hi everyone — quick update on two small but important clarifications to our family-related travel & leave policies. These clarifications are effective 2026-10-01 and are meant to reduce surprises for employees who travel with dependents or need short emergency leave while traveling. Full details: https://intranet.redwood.com/policies/family-travel-leave (TL;DR below)

Carlos Vega: Thanks Imani. What changed?

Imani Brooks: Two clarifications: 1) When a dependent must travel with you for a work trip due to medical or legal reasons, you may submit a "Family Travel Support" claim (code FAM-TRAV) for reasonable incremental costs (extra airfare, one hotel room, short-term local care) up to $600 per trip. 2) Employees may choose to use PTO concurrently with short-term Travel Emergency Leave for up to 7 days per event; this does not extend unpaid leave entitlements.

Samir (Legal): A reminder on documentation: include a brief justification tying the expense to the business trip. Do NOT upload sensitive medical records; a manager-attested statement will suffice. For international receipts, include a currency conversion proof (bank or card transaction). Visa fees for dependents are excluded unless pre-approved by People Ops for critical business reasons.

Priya Nair: Submission: use Concur -> Expenses -> New -> FAM-TRAV. Attach receipts and manager approval screenshot. Payroll will review tax treatment per region and flag items as taxable where required. Typical turnaround: 3-7 business days.

Payroll Team: Note for submitters: if your country treats the reimbursement as taxable, we will notify you and handle withholding in the next payroll cycle. Include your payroll region in the expense notes to speed up reviews.

hr-bot: :information_source: "Family Travel & Short Emergency Leave clarifications" published at https://intranet.redwood.com/policies/family-travel-leave. Effective date: 2026-10-01. Questions: people-ops@redwood.com

Carlos Vega: Appreciate the heads-up — will forward to my team.
